questions.q: What distinction does the summary give Israel among the world’s nations?
a: It has more startups per person than any other country
It has the largest population in the Middle East
It exports more oil than its neighbors
It spends the least on research and development
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Israel has roughly one startup for every 2,000 citizens, the highest rate per capita.

questions.q: What does the Hebrew term chutzpah describe in the summary?
a: The confidence to stand up for your own ideas
The patience to wait for the right opportunity
The skill of negotiating a lower price
The habit of avoiding conflict with superiors
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses the PayPal meeting, where Israelis criticized the CEO’s practices, to illustrate chutzpah.

questions.q: Where does the summary trace Israelis’ habit of asking questions?
a: A long tradition of rabbis debating the meaning of the Bible
The country’s compulsory military service
The influence of European business schools
A national law requiring open debate
questions.why: Lesson 2 says centuries of open argument over scripture carried into the culture of entrepreneurship.

questions.q: Why does the Israeli army keep few senior officers?
a: To push lower-ranking soldiers to take initiative
To save money on military salaries
To make room for foreign advisors
To avoid public criticism of the army
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the flat structure exists so soldiers at lower levels take responsibility for their work.

questions.q: How did political isolation shape Israel’s economy?
a: It pushed the country toward software and digital goods that cross borders
It forced the country to rely on oil exports
It made the country dependent on foreign factories
It slowed the growth of its technology sector
questions.why: Lesson 3 says boycotts and travel limits pushed Israel into a knowledge economy early.
